question: What recent experiments have verified the existence of the Casimir force at the micro- and nanoscale?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: Identifies the experiment measuring non-monotonic Casimir forces between lithographically defined and etched silicon nanostructures with arrays of T-shaped protrusions.
examples: First measurement of a non-monotonic Casimir force between complex-shaped nanostructures
T-shaped protrusion arrays yielded a Casimir force with two maxima, a minimum, and a sharp increase
Lithographic definition ensured automatic alignment of the interacting surfaces

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: Specifies that the gap was controlled by an integrated comb actuator and the force gradient was sensed via resonance frequency shifts of a vibrating silicon beam, with electrostatic contributions minimized.
examples: Comb actuator set the distance; vibrating beam detected the force gradient
Electrostatic contribution was minimized by setting Ve = Vo(d)
Resonance frequency shifts of the oscillating beam measured the force gradient

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: States that measured force gradients agreed with parameter-free Casimir calculations (boundary-element/fluctuating-surface-currents method, e.g., SCUFF-EM) accounting for finite silicon conductivity, with no fitting parameters.
examples: SCUFF-EM calculations with finite conductivity reproduced the data with no fitting parameters
The calculation reproduced all main features including the non-monotonic behavior

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Describes the experiment demonstrating phonon heat transfer across a vacuum gap of several hundred nanometers between two Si3N4 films, each coupled to reservoirs at different temperatures, with the Casimir interaction acting as a coupling spring between their vibrational modes.
examples: Quantum fluctuations mediated heat flow across a vacuum between two membranes
The Casimir force acted as a coupling spring between phonon modes of the two films
Hot and cold reservoirs drove heat flow through the vacuum gap

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: Explains that distance-dependent temperature deviations of the films' vibrational modes from their reservoirs, consistent with Casimir force calculations, confirmed the interaction.
examples: At small separations the vibrational-mode temperatures deviated from reservoir temperatures
Temperature deviations grew at smaller gaps where the Casimir force is stronger
Observed temperature deviations matched Casimir calculations

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: Includes the high-vacuum experiment with two closely spaced cantilevers, motion monitored by fiber interferometers, where the measured force gradient matched theoretical Casimir predictions.
examples: Force gradient between two cantilevers in high vacuum matched the calculated Casimir gradient
Fiber interferometers monitored cantilever displacement

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: Discusses methodological caveats such as non-uniform T-protrusions, patch potentials, imperfect sidewalls, and the negligible thermal correction at 4 K (zeroth Matsubara term <0.3%).
examples: Discrepancies attributed to patch potentials and geometry variation between unit cells
At 4 K the thermal correction was negligible (<0.3% from the zeroth Matsubara term)
Imperfect sidewalls were cited as error sources

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Adds context such as study years, implications for nanomechanical components with non-conventional shapes, and further physics demonstrated (exceptional points, nonreciprocal energy transfer).
examples: First step toward exploiting Casimir forces in complex-shaped nanomechanics
Modulating one cantilever achieved exceptional points and nonreciprocal energy transfer
